subject: fix(web): make the machines page's tests independent of what else the suite started
instruction:
fix(web): make the machines page's tests independent of what else the suite started

Both branches of this page were being decided by ambient cluster state. A full `mix test`
run starts dozens of distributed nodes, and `Ouroboros.Cluster`'s directory remembers every
one of them, so `fleet.status` on the suite host answers a 44-machine roster rather than the
no-fleet shape it answers when this file runs alone. The page was right both times — it
rendered the roster the runtime gave it, with the correct chips — but three tests asserted
the empty state and failed the moment they ran after anything else.

So the empty state is rendered as a component, which is the only way to reach that branch
on a host that happens to be clustered, and the live page instead asserts the thing that is
true either way: its verdict is the runtime's own, computed by the predicate `fleet.doctor`
uses for the same question (`cluster.ex:1771`). The doctor assertion moves off "healthy" —
a verdict that depends on those same leftover nodes — onto the headline's own words and the
first check's id.

Also drops the backticks from the empty state's prose in favour of `<code>`, which is what
the rest of this surface marks a command up as.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - the page shows whichever branch fleet.status actually put it in
  - no page state offers an add control
  - refresh re-reads fleet.status and asks the doctor nothing

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place. Work only inside this worktree.
